title: Visibility rubric
description: The rubric for judging how far a tool gives the system visibility of an activity, and how far the venture owns the record (EE-222), which Naive ships at packages/naive/src/functions/it/visibility-rubric.json. Each criterion asks one question about a tool and an activity, says why it matters, describes the levels of a 0 to 4 scale and carries a default weight that is an unvalidated prior a venture overrides under visibility in naive.config.json. A gate criterion rules out a candidate scored 0 on it; a blind_spot criterion scored 0 means the tool leaves the activity unrecorded, which is flagged and never rules a candidate out, because only a person does that. A channel says how an activity is performed, and therefore what must capture it, told from the words of its statement as an activity's kind is (EE-179). A tool kind is a kind of tool and never a vendor, with the prior scores Naive ships for it. A score never decides: packages/naive/src/engine/visibility-rubric.ts ranks candidates and a person chooses. packages/naive/src/checks/check-visibility-rubric.ts checks what this schema cannot: weights that sum to 1, sources that are reference ids, decisions that are EE ids, channels and tool kinds that resolve, and examples that name only the rubric's criteria.

tie_band.description: Two candidates whose totals (0 to 1) differ by no more than this are reported as tied, not ordered.

question.description: The one question to ask about a tool and the activity it would cover.

why.description: Why the answer can change the choice.

iso25010.description: The ISO/IEC 25010:2023 product quality characteristics the criterion serves. A criterion the standard does not cover names none.

levels.description: What a score means on this criterion. Scores 0 and 4 must be described; packages/naive/src/checks/check-visibility-rubric.ts checks it.

weight.description: The default weight, an unvalidated prior. The criteria's weights sum to 1; a venture may set others under visibility in naive.config.json.

gate.description: True when a score of 0 rules a candidate out, whatever its other scores.

blind_spot.description: True when a score of 0 means the tool leaves the activity unrecorded. Such a candidate is flagged as a blind spot and still ranked: only a person rules it out.

decisions.description: EE decisions the criterion draws on.

channels.description: How an activity is performed, and therefore what must capture it. Read in order: the first channel whose clauses the activity's statement meets is its channel, and the one marked default takes an activity whose words meet none.

record.description: What a record of an activity on this channel looks like.

when.description: Clauses on the words of the activity's statement, as the activity catalog's kinds hold them (EE-179): the first word is its verb and the rest are its terms. A statement meets a clause when its verb is one of the verbs and one of its terms is one of the terms. An unvalidated prior.

default.description: True for the one channel that takes an activity whose words meet no clause. It names no clauses.

tool_kinds.description: The tool kinds that could capture this channel, by id.
A kind of tool, never a vendor: Naive names no vendor in code, and a venture's own connection record (it/connections/<id>.json) names its system.

kind.description: What kind of tool it is, in plain words, with no product or company name.

captures.description: The channels this kind of tool could capture, by id.

scores.description: The prior score on each criterion, an unvalidated prior for the kind and not a measurement of any product.

why.description: The reason for each score, citing a reference, a decision or a file.

rated.description: Who gave the scores, when and from what.

examples.description: Worked examples: an activity that must be visible, the candidates considered and the choice a person made.

activity.description: The activity that must be visible, and where it comes from.

channel.description: The channel it is performed on, by id.

weights.description: Weights for this activity that replace the rubric's defaults, by criterion id. A weight of 0 leaves the criterion out, unscored.

must.description: Must-haves: the lowest score a candidate needs on a criterion. A candidate below it is ruled out.

candidates.description: The tool kinds considered, by id. Each must capture the example's channel.

chosen.description: The candidate a person chose. It may differ from the top score.

decided_by.description: The EE decisions that record the choice.

rated.description: Who judged the example, when and from what. The choice is the decisions'.
